beats.vo: A shipwreck. A lump of corroded bronze. And inside it... the oldest computer on Earth.
This is the Antikythera mechanism. Thirty bronze gears, built twenty-one hundred years ago.
Turn the crank... and the sky moves.
One gear has two hundred and twenty-three teeth.
Exactly the number of months between eclipses.
So it predicted eclipses... decades in advance.
But the real genius is hidden right here.
Two gears, slightly off-center... with a pin sliding inside a slot.
That makes the Moon speed up and slow down... exactly like the real one.
Nothing this complex appears again... for fourteen hundred years.
Should I rebuild the eclipse dial next... or the Roman crane? Comment A or B.

metadata.description:
The Antikythera mechanism: 30+ bronze gears that predicted eclipses with a 223-tooth gear, and a pin-and-slot trick that reproduces the Moon's changing speed. Nothing this complex appears again for ~1,400 years.

3D reconstruction by Ancient Tech. Comment A or B to pick the next machine.

Sources: Freeth et al., Nature 2006/2008; Antikythera Mechanism Research Project.
